props.gloss_en: on three occasions the priests raise their hands whenever they pray, and on some of them four times a day -- shacharit, musaf, mincha and neila
this [the mishnah's four times] is the statement of R' Meir
shacharit and musaf have the raising of the hands
mincha [of a fast] does not have the raising of the hands
neila does not have the raising of the hands
R' Meir: mincha too has the raising of the hands
neila has the raising of the hands (R' Meir; R' Yosei)
who are the Sages [of Rabba bar Avuh's dictum]? it is R' Yehuda
R' Meir (per the stam): every day the priests do not spread their hands at mincha because of drunkenness
R' Meir (per the stam): today [a fast] there is no drunkenness
R' Yehuda (per the stam): shacharit and musaf, where drunkenness is not common on every day -- the Rabbis did not decree about them
R' Yehuda (per the stam): mincha and neila, where drunkenness is common on every day -- the Rabbis decreed about them
R' Yosei (per the stam): mincha, which exists every day -- the Rabbis decreed about it
R' Yosei (per the stam): neila, which does not exist every day -- the Rabbis did not decree about it
Rav: the halakha follows R' Meir
R' Yochanan: the people act in accordance with R' Meir
Rava: the custom is in accordance with R' Meir
the one who said 'halakha' means: we expound it in the public lecture
the one who said 'custom' means: we do not expound it, but we do instruct it
the one who said 'the people act' means: we do not instruct it, but if one does it, it is done, and we do not make him go back
Rav Nachman: the halakha follows R' Yosei
nowadays the priests spread their hands at the mincha of a fast
since they spread [their hands] near sunset, it is like the neila prayer
according to all, at any rate, a drunk is forbidden to raise his hands
bar Kappara: just as the nazirite is forbidden wine, so the priest who blesses is forbidden wine
R' Yitzchak: just as the ministering priest is permitted grape-pits, so the priest who blesses is permitted grape-pits
R' Yitzchak's verse: 'to minister to Him and to bless in His name' (Devarim 10:8)
they are rabbinic supports (asmachtot), and [are juxtaposed] to leniency
